rationale: Correct the existing DataBank record in place and resolve the reciprocal DataBank Holdings candidate to the same canonical company. DataBank's live investor page, transaction releases and current filings support seven current manager-universe associations: DigitalBridge, Swiss Life Asset Managers, IMCO, AustralianSuper, Northleaf Capital Partners, Ardian and CBRE Investment Management. Northleaf, Ardian and CBRE Investment Management are omitted from the current record and must be added; the existing Swiss Life period must be corrected to Swiss Life Asset Managers. DigitalBridge directly disclosed a continuing 7.8% stake after the January 2025 secondary. The 2022 consortium acquired a collective 35% interest, but individual percentages were not disclosed, so that aggregate is not allocated among Swiss Life, Northleaf or Ardian. DataBank brands TIAA's investment manager as Nuveen, while the TIAA Real Estate Account directly reports a 14.8% beneficial stake through DigitalBridge Zeus vehicles. That evidence does not support a separate Nuveen Infrastructure period, and InfraBridge has no separate DataBank equity evidence. TIAA, EDF Invest and TJC are current co-owner context outside the supplied manager universe and are retained in the narrative rather than added as manager-task ownership rows. The January 2025 secondary did not identify every seller, so no other period is retired by inference. No later full sale or signed pending exit was identified through August 18, 2026.

beforeImage.name: DataBank
beforeImage.description: DataBank provides colocation, interconnection, and managed infrastructure services for enterprise, cloud, and artificial-intelligence workloads. Its customers include enterprises, hyperscale users, and network counterparties that require data-center capacity, connectivity, and related managed services across multiple U.S. markets. The operating model is asset-heavy because the business owns and operates data-center facilities and critical power and cooling infrastructure, with revenues generated through long-term capacity, colocation, and service contracts. AustralianSuper describes the platform as one of the larger North American data-center operators, and public disclosures in 2024 referenced more than 65 data centers across 27 key markets and a build-out plan exceeding 850 MW of additional capacity. DataBank was founded in 2005, DigitalBridge has been a long-term sponsor since 2016, and AustralianSuper became a significant minority owner through the 2024 equity raise.

milestones.event: DataBank was founded in Dallas, Texas.
Digital Bridge acquired DataBank from Avista Capital Partners and launched the platform as its inaugural data-center investment.
Swiss Life Asset Managers and EDF Invest agreed to acquire a minority stake in DataBank.
DataBank completed the first phase of its recapitalization, with the Swiss Life-led investor consortium and IMCO investing in the platform.
DataBank announced an approximately $2.0 billion equity raise led by AustralianSuper, including a $1.5 billion commitment from the fund.
DigitalBridge announced participation in a new DataBank financing and disclosed that it would retain an ownership stake.

afterImage.name: DataBank
afterImage.description: DataBank Holdings, Ltd. operates a nationwide digital-infrastructure platform providing colocation, interconnection, cloud, storage, managed security and compliance services to enterprise, cloud, content and technology customers. Founded in Dallas in 2005, DataBank was acquired from Avista by a DigitalBridge-led group in July 2016 and has since expanded through acquisitions, development and multiple recapitalizations. DataBank reported more than 70 data centers in more than 25 markets, 20 interconnection hubs, more than 2,200 customers and more than $1 billion of revenue in May 2026. The current manager-universe ownership roster is DigitalBridge, Swiss Life Asset Managers, IMCO, AustralianSuper, Northleaf Capital Partners, Ardian and CBRE Investment Management. DigitalBridge disclosed a 7.8% continuing stake after the January 2025 secondary. TIAA's Real Estate Account separately disclosed a 14.8% beneficial stake through DigitalBridge Zeus vehicles; DataBank brands that relationship as Nuveen, but it is not evidenced as a Nuveen Infrastructure investment. EDF Invest and TJC are also current investors outside the supplied manager universe. Individual data centers, campuses, interconnection hubs and acquired operating assets remain within the single DataBank platform boundary. No later full sale or signed pending exit was identified through August 18, 2026.

milestones.event: DataBank Ltd. was founded in the former Federal Reserve Bank Building in downtown Dallas, Texas.
Digital Bridge acquired DataBank from Avista Capital Partners with TIAA, Allstate Investments and The Edgewater Funds, launching its first data-center platform.

Colony Capital purchased $185 million of secondary DataBank interests from Edgewater and Allstate; Edgewater exited, Allstate retained half of its prior interest and the Nuveen-branded TIAA investment continued.

A Swiss Life-led consortium with EDF Invest, Northleaf and Ardian closed a collective 35% DataBank interest for approximately $1.5 billion; IMCO then agreed to invest up to $450 million in the continuing recapitalization.

DataBank announced an approximately $2.0 billion equity raise led by AustralianSuper's $1.5 billion commitment, which would make AustralianSuper a significant minority owner; DataBank now lists it as a current investor.

DataBank announced a $250 million TJC investment and an approximately $600 million secondary share sale; DigitalBridge disclosed that the transaction would adjust its continuing DataBank stake to 7.8%.
